cues: Short-day plants, such as chrysanthemum, soybean and Xanthium, flower only when the night is longer than a critical length.
Long-day plants, such as wheat, radish and spinach, flower only when the night is shorter than a critical length.
Suppose, as an example, both have a critical night of about twelve hours.
Day-neutral plants such as tomato do not care.
